statusVocabulary.native-provider: A registered native provider in src/registry/providers.json implements the lens's detection rules.
statusVocabulary.partial-native-provider: One or more native providers or scanners cover part of the lens; the gaps field names what is not covered.
statusVocabulary.card-only: Draft semantic pattern cards on the reasoning.security lens (native_providers/reasoning/pattern_cards.rs) are the only engine consumer; no deterministic detector exists.
statusVocabulary.not-implemented: No engine consumer. The lens is a planning label only and supports no coverage claim.

lenses.description: Credential material in repository artifacts.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors in src/registry/providers.json (source and configuration files).

lenses.gaps: Git-history and client-bundle exposure depend on the history and secrets providers' own coverage.

lenses.description: Injection into interpreter, query, template, and process sinks.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors in src/registry/providers.json.

lenses.gaps: Native rule coverage is command injection and unsafe deserialization only; SQL, NoSQL, template, LDAP, and XML injection rely on external scanner rulesets and reasoning.security, and are not lens-owned.

lenses.description: Authentication/TLS/debug fail-open defaults.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors in src/registry/providers.json (source and configuration files).

lenses.gaps: Framework-specific defaults beyond the three native rules are not covered.

lenses.description: CI/CD event, permission, secret, and release trust.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors: workflow and agent-source paths in src/registry/providers.json.

lenses.gaps: Cloud, IaC, and release-signing trust paths are outside this lens.

lenses.description: Workspace config, plugin, tool, and process trust.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors plus path evidence for the workspace-trust group (.env, hooks, project configuration, MCP and plugin discovery).

lenses.gaps: Pre-trust execution in non-agent CLIs and editors is covered only by the draft card.

lenses.description: Object, function, role, and tenant authorization.

applicability.evidence: Always-on core card on reasoning.security.

lenses.gaps: No deterministic detector; IDOR, function-level, and mass-assignment review are reasoning-only.

lenses.description: Authentication, recovery, session, and token lifecycle.

applicability.evidence: Path evidence for the auth-session group (auth, login, session, mfa, oauth, jwt, recovery tokens).

lenses.gaps: No deterministic detector; session-store and identity-provider behavior outside the source stays unknown.

lenses.description: Workflow invariants, idempotency, and state-transition authority.

applicability.evidence: Admin-workflow group path evidence; the commerce and webhook cards are owned by the data-safety lens and apply under its own trigger.

lenses.gaps: Two of the three cards belong to data-safety, not reasoning.security.

lenses.description: SSRF, filesystem, upload, parser, and serialization boundaries.

applicability.evidence: Provider rules plus path evidence for the SSRF/egress group.

lenses.gaps: Upload and archive boundaries are not covered by any provider or card.

lenses.description: Browser, CORS, cache, proxy, and HTTP protocol controls.

applicability.evidence: Path evidence for the HTTP proxy/cache group (proxy, gateway, nginx, cache, ingress configuration).

lenses.gaps: CORS, CSP, and CSRF review are reasoning-only with no card; framing disagreement needs both tiers in the source.

lenses.description: Cryptography, identity protocols, data protection, and privacy.

applicability.evidence: Provider rule for TLS verification; privacy card is owned by data-safety.

lenses.gaps: Weak-primitive, randomness, and encryption-at-rest checks have no detector.

lenses.description: Supply-chain, developer-machine, automation, and update trust.

applicability.evidence: Provider selectors in src/registry/providers.json.

lenses.gaps: Developer-machine trust is covered only through the workspace-trust lens.

lenses.description: Untrusted content influencing model decisions.

applicability.evidence: Agent, skill, hook, and MCP path selector.

lenses.gaps: Application prompt assembly outside agent and skill files is reasoning-only.

lenses.description: Agent tool authority, identity scope, approval, and side-effect bounds.

applicability.evidence: Agent, skill, hook, and MCP path selector.

lenses.gaps: Approval and identity-scope review are reasoning-only.

lenses.description: RAG poisoning, memory abuse, grounding, and evaluation integrity.

applicability.evidence: Path evidence for the AI memory/RAG group (rag, embedding, vector store, retrieval, memory).

lenses.gaps: Evaluation-integrity review has no card.

lenses.description: Smart-contract access control, reentrancy, and oracle trust.

applicability.evidence: Applies only on strong path evidence (.sol, .vy, foundry or hardhat configuration); excluded only when every selected path is recognized source with none.

lenses.gaps: Signature replay, upgradeability, and bridge assumptions are not carded.

lenses.description: Embedded and IoT firmware update authentication, debug interfaces, and device keys.

applicability.evidence: Applies only on strong path evidence (firmware, bootloader, platformio, sdkconfig, device-tree, linker scripts).

lenses.gaps: Native parser safety and radio configuration are not carded.

lenses.description: ICS/OT control-protocol authentication and safety interlocks (repository and configuration review only).

applicability.evidence: Applies only on strong path evidence (PLC project files, modbus, opcua, dnp3, iec61850 paths).

lenses.gaps: Never performs live probing; segmentation and remote-maintenance review are not carded.
